To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the rp-process in X-ray bursts does no longer end at Z greater than or equals 32 but proceeds to Z greater than or = 36, (ii) the production of p-nuclei via the rp-process in accretion disk around low mass black hole is enhanced and (iii) the rp-process energy release in the Z less than or equals 34 region cannot be neglected for accretion disk scenarios

the rp-process nucleosynthetic flow in X-ray bursts and low-mass black hole environments is not terminated at Z = 32, but proceeds to the A similar to 80-100 mass range where large observed solar system overabundances of light p-nucleis are observed.
the rp-process nucleosyntheis of nuclei in the mass range 80-100 is strongly influenced by 2p-captures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nucleosynthesis of the light p-nucleosynthesis of the rp-process.
the nucleosynthesis of the heavy p-process isotopes in the mass range A = 70-130, i. e. in the region between the proton drip line and the valley of beta-stability.
the nucleosynthesis of heavy nuclei via the rapid proton capture process (rp-process) in X-ray bursts and accretion disks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rp-process nucleosynthetic scenario in X-ray bursts is still not well understood.
we are still far from being able to make a definite prediction of nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts and accretion disks.
the nuclear structure uncertainties in the rp-process are still large, but the current uncertainties in the nuclear input parameters are small compared to the ones in the X-ray burst models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rp-process is very sensitive to the nuclear structure of the nuclei in the region of the proton drip line and that a large number of new experimental and theoretical data is needed to further constrain the nuclear models.
the rp-process is a promising mechanism for the production of light p-nucleosynthesis.
nuclear structure uncertainties in the rp-process are large, but the uncertainties are not so large as to make the results useless.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rp-process in X-ray bursts and accretion disks is much more efficient in producing p-nuclei than previously thought, because of 2p capture reactions.
the rp-process in X-ray bursts does indeed end in the Z greater than 36 region, as was previously assumed.
the rp-process in X-ray bursts and in the accretion disks of black holes does not end in Z less than or equal to32 region as previously assumed but proceeds into the Z greater or equal to 34 region.
